For non-member states, consular legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin, followed by authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of that country.

Hague Apostille: Issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-member states, consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission in the country of origin, preceded by authentication by the local competent authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Notarization by a Korean notary, then apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-member states, notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company's founders or legal representative (notarized by a Korean notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Notarization by a Korean notary, then apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State in the US). For non-member states, consular legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own list of designated persons under the AML/CFT Act. Additionally, all beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must be screened for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Korean Financial Services Commission. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and continuously thereafter, with risk-based frequency. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. The screening process must include name matching with fuzzy logic to account for transliteration variations, and must be performed against both English and Korean script versions of names. Any positive hit triggers immediate escalation to the compliance officer and a risk-based decision, with potential filing of a suspicious transaction report (STR) to KoFIU within 24 hours if warranted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) script. For foreign entities, a phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required, and the English name may be used as a secondary name. The name must comply with the Commercial Act (상법) and the Enforcement Decree, which require a four-tier naming convention: (1) the corporate form indicator (e.g., '유한회사' for LLC), (2) the unique name, (3) the business purpose, and (4) the registered office address. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Foreign-language names are permitted only as a secondary name, and the Korean name must be used for all official filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, principally Articles 543, 544, 546, 548, 560, 561, 565, 567 and 568, which govern Yuhan Hoesa (a limited liability company), together with Articles 289 to 292, 317, 318, 383, 388, 393, 397 and 398 as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 543(2); the Corporate Registration Act; and the registration and dispute procedures administered by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court (Deungsogso) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Yuhan Hoesa, within the court system administered by the National Court Administration of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing may be made through the Korean Court Internet Registration Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa, supported by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, and culminating in the issuance of a Certificate of Registered Matters (Deung-gi sa-hang jeung-myeong) and a corporate seal certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The capital amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid into a bank account opened in the company's name before the incorporation registration is submitted. A bank-issued certificate of capital deposit must accompany the registration; no blocked escrow account is required. The fixed court filing fee component is approximately USD 35, and registration tax on the actual contributed capital is payable at the applicable local schedule.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: Hometax (hometax.go.kr); export/customs administration: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean entity: first execute entity formation before the Commercial Registry; the foreign company must then file a Business Registration Application (with articles of incorporation, foreign certificate of incorporation/analogous legal existence certificate, board resolution appointing an in-country representative or tax representative, proof of domestic place of business, and power of attorney) with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the domestic place of business, or online through Hometax. The NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number used for corporate income tax, VAT/payroll withholdings, and e-Tax invoice issuance. If the foreign entity has no domestic place of business but is within the scope of Korean VAT for remote/electronic services, register as a foreign non-resident VAT operator through Hometax, identify a Korean tax representative, and obtain the NTS-issued Business Registration Number under the foreign-registration procedure; domestic and non-resident VAT registrations are mandatory before the first taxable supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Yuhan Hoesa LLC is taxable at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through eligibility)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Korean tax classification is statutory; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections). A foreign corporation can elect to appoint a tax representative for procedural compliance, and a qualifying wholly-owned domestic subsidiary may elect consolidated corporate tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act, but no US-style entity classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory turnover threshold; VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable business activity in Korea. The simplified-taxpayer ceiling of KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable supplies (KRW 48,000,000 for certain prescribed businesses) affects simplified tax calculation but does not exempt registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national e-Tax Invoice administration through Hometax: every registered VAT operator issuing a tax invoice must transmit the e-Tax Invoice into Hometax (portal, EDI, or government-certified open API) no later than the day after issuance; NTS validates issuer registration, buyer confirmation, and invoice amount in real time. Retail and prescribed consumer-service operations must use approved cash-receipt (credit-card / cash-receipt device) equipment and transmit those transactions to NTS by the following business day. Korea does not currently apply fiscal stamping; anti-fraud controls are supported by NTS Big-Data cross-matching between purchase/supply e-invoices, customs declarations, and foreign-exchange receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for 0% VAT if the goods are sold to a non-resident purchaser, physically exported under a Korea Customs Service electronic export declaration, invoiced at zero VAT, and paid for by the foreign buyer in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Export of services is zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident and the services are deemed consumed outside Korea, consideration is received in foreign currency, and the prescribed export-evidence package is retained. International transport and related services qualify as zero-rated by statute; offshore digital services sold to Korean consumers remain within the domestic VAT scope and are not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic Export Declaration / cargo clearance printout with export entry number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing export of the goods from Korea to the foreign destination
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and HS-code master data matching the export declaration and 0% VAT e-Tax invoice
0% VAT e-Tax Invoice addressed to the foreign buyer and transmitted through Hometax
Foreign exchange bank certificate of export-proceeds collection (bank-issued foreign currency receipt certificate equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS examination will verify the export declaration, B/L, and foreign-exchange receipt trail; if the 0% claim lacks documentary support, is not substantiated, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the prescribed period without an approved extension, the NTS will reassess 10% VAT on the unproven export revenue, impose statutory penalties for false/unsubstantiated tax invoices and unfaithful return, add interest/overdue amounts under the National Tax Collection Act, and can refer the matter for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Refunds erroneously paid are retroactively clawed back with interest; the fraud limitation period of ten years applies, and concealment/false documentation will not benefit from any shortened assessment period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (Central Bank of the Republic of Korea), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a fundamentally current-account convertible regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA). Current account settlements in respect of medical device consulting fees, licensing royalties, and trade-related disbursements are generally free from prior approval, provided that the underlying contract and supporting documentation are retained. Capital account transactions are largely liberalized under a positive-list system; declared direct investments, equity injections, and intra-company loans may be routed through authorized foreign exchange banks with post-transaction reporting. There are no surrender requirements compelling mandatory conversion of export proceeds into Korean won; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts. Profit remittances and dividend outflows are permitted after verification of accumulated undistributed earnings, audited financial statements, and valid tax clearance certificates. During balance-of-payments stress, the Bank of Korea may reinstate emergency approval measures, but such measures have not been actively invoked in the current cycle. The central bank operates the Foreign Exchange Information System to monitor large transactions and ensure statistical reporting. Non-resident LLCs are permitted to hold KRW current accounts and foreign-currency accounts, but full convertibility is contingent on clean AML/KYC onboarding and submission of purpose-of-remittance codes. The overall assessment is high convertibility for transactional flows with moderate compliance friction only for suspicious or unusually structured capital injections.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 26 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be received and settled, deposited in a foreign currency account, or sold to an authorized foreign exchange bank within one year from the date of exportation. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; the exporter may elect to retain the foreign exchange liquidity in a bank-operated foreign currency account. However, the settlement must be reported to the foreign exchange bank within the applicable reporting window, and any overdue export proceeds require an extension from the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very low viability for offshore digital EMI providers. Foreign electronic money issuers and non-bank fintech institutions are not authorized to open resident Korean won settlement accounts or act as primary clearing members of the local payment system. The Electronic Financial Transactions Act requires a domestic FSC license for e-money issuance, and no passporting regime exists for overseas EMIs. At the treasury stage, such providers may be used solely as ancillary payment initiators, but they cannot host the entity’s operating liquidity or satisfy Korean foreign exchange bank reporting obligations. A Tier-1 Korean commercial bank remains mandatory for statutory inbound capital verification and outbound trade settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is required. Korean banks, guided by the Financial Services Commission and Korea FIU AML guidelines, do not recognize remote consular proxy opening for a newly formed foreign-owned LLC. At least one statutory director, or a formally appointed authorized signatory with a corporate power of attorney, must appear in person at the main corporate banking branch with the original corporate seal, passport, alien registration card or foreign ID, and certified constitutional documents. Remote notarization by a Korean consulate may support document authentication but does not waive the branch interview requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity caused by layered foreign holding companies or nominee shareholder arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate register excerpt evidencing the complete shareholding chain to natural persons, individual passports of all UBOs, audited financial statements of the immediate parent, source-of-wealth declaration, six months of source-of-funds bank statements, and a sworn affidavit affirming the absence of nominee shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsupported or unexplained initial capital injection into an entity with no local employment or physical operational footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital amount and business purpose, notarized investment contract with counterparties, capital verification certificate from the receiving Korean bank, sponsor bank reference letter, personal or corporate bank statements showing the provenance of funds, and a detailed treasury plan mapping funds to FDA/CE regulatory projects.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payables flowing to high-risk medical technology suppliers or jurisdictions with elevated sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements, jurisdiction-specific end-user certificates, export/import declarations, medical device registration files, regulatory consulting invoices, shipping or delivery documentation, and independent third-party sanctions screening reports covering each counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and political exposure screening hits or PEP matches in the Korean financial intelligence database
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full OFAC, UN, EU, FSS, and Bank of Korea watch-list screening reports, attestation of non-involvement by each UBO and director, PEP declaration form, institutional ownership chart illustrating no government or state-owned beneficiary control, and legal counsel opinion confirming no targeted conduct.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT with the relevant Korean foreign exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment or equity participation. The remitter should clearly identify the Korean LLC, reference the capital contribution resolution, and submit the remittance to an authorized foreign-exchange bank. The receiving bank will issue a certificate of receipt, which is then filed with the customs and statistics authorities as capital verification. Funds must not arrive in mixed tranches or under trade settlement descriptions; each injection should match the formal board resolution and tax filing number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and consulting disbursements should be settled primarily through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the Korean LLC’s operating currency account. For goods-related medical device transactions, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections may be used when required by the supplier financing structure. All settlements must be supported by the underlying invoice, import declaration, or consulting contract and reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System for amounts subject to monitoring thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won forward contracts for current account exposures
Currency swaps with authorized foreign exchange banks to manage funding-currency mismatches
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for non-resident hedging of medium-term receivables
Option strategies limited to plain vanilla puts and calls on KRW versus USD/EUR under bank product eligibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Value-Added Tax return for the preceding July-December supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hometax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the year immediately following the preceding calendar year for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT non-filing and underpayment attract statutory additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act, including 10% of the unpaid tax for ordinary non-filing and a daily late-payment surcharge; persistent non-compliance allows NTS seizure of bank accounts and receivables, revocation of the business registration, and may support a court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement, notes) submitted to the ordinary general meeting of members and retained in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General meeting of members of Yuhan Hoesa; records retained at the registered office and available for inspection by the Commercial Registry Court, NTS, and members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa the ordinary members' meeting and financial statement approval must occur no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary general meeting or to approve financial statements does not automatically cause administrative strike-off, but each managing member may face statutory administrative fines under the Commercial Act; delayed approval also blocks timely corporate tax filing and exposes the company to the NTS non-filing and late-payment penalty regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified public accountant external audit report (required only if statutory audit threshold is exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Appointed Korea-registered CPA auditor; report is submitted to the annual members' meeting and must accompany financial statements and the corporate income tax return when the company is subject to mandatory external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the audit must be completed before the ordinary general meeting and in all cases by March 31 of the following year; auditor appointment must be made within the statutory period after confirming the previous year's asset threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to obtain a mandatory audit report under the Act on External Audit and Accounting Standards may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 23,000); unaudited or incomplete financial statements may be rejected by NTS for corporate tax purposes, and repeated non-compliance is evidence for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hometax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the third month following close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa the due date is March 31 of the following year, subject to a statutory extension of up to two months in prescribed cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ordinary non-filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; fraudulent underreporting or non-filing triggers 40%; late payment accrues a statutory daily surcharge; prolonged failure permits NTS seizure of assets and business registration cancellation, and unresolved corporate liabilities may lead to a court-ordered compulsory liquidation or membership-equity forfeiture in a strike-off proceeding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the principal business place (Si/Gun/Gu) through the WeTax local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 of the year following the fiscal year-end for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, being the month after the NTS corporate income tax deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquency carries local additional tax penalties, including a 20% penalty for non-filing, 40% for fraudulent underreporting, and a daily late-payment surcharge; local government may attach company property, suspend the business permit through collection procedures, and seek judicial dissolution for chronic delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preliminary Value-Added Tax return for the January-March supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hometax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 of the current calendar year for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or late preliminary VAT filing attracts the VAT Act additional tax on the short-paid or unreported amount and daily late-payment interest; continued delinquency is an NTS collection and business-registration revocation trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Value-Added Tax return for the January-June supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hometax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the current calendar year for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underpayment penalties apply under the Value-Added Tax Act, including additional tax on unpaid VAT and daily default interest; persistent default can trigger NTS distraint and a court application for corporate dissolution/strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim corporate income tax prepayment return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hometax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: August 31 of the current calendar year for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, being two months after the first six months of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the interim prepayment or to pay the required amount subjects the company to statutory additional tax and late-payment surcharge on the unpaid interim tax; NTS may enforce collection and ultimately cancel the business registration or move for compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim local corporate income tax prepayment return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the principal business place (Si/Gun/Gu) through the WeTax local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: September 30 of the current calendar year for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, being the month after the NTS interim prepayment deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax additional taxes and daily late-payment surcharges accrue on the unpaid interim local corporate income tax; local authorities may attach assets and treat chronic delinquency as grounds for business closure and corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preliminary Value-Added Tax return for the July-September supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hometax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: October 25 of the current calendar year for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT penalty rules apply on unreported or underpaid preliminary VAT, including statutory additional tax and daily default surcharge; sustained non-payment permits NTS enforced collection and revocation of business registration, followed by court-ordered dissolution/strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and update (Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges, and minute book review)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of Yuhan Hoesa; records must be available for on-site inspection by the court registration office, NTS, and members upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the ordinary general meeting, and no later than March 31 for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa; each register must be continuously accurate throughout the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing statutory registers expose managing members to Commercial Act administrative fines and personal liability for damages suffered by the company or members; repeated non-compliance is not a direct automatic strike-off but is admissible evidence in a Compulsory Dissolution Order proceeding before the District Court.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is mandated to undergo an independent statutory audit under the Act on External Audit and Accounting Standards if its total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national CIT, producing a top combined effective rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea offers foreign-invested high-tech FDI tax holidays under Article 121.2 of the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, typically 100% corporate tax exemption for five years and 50% exemption for the following two years for qualifying projects; R&D tax credits are available for research on new growth-generating technologies; no Korean patent box regime currently exists, but technology-transfer income may qualify for tax deferral or partial exclusion under special tax provisions; free-zone and Free Economic Zone incentives can further reduce the effective rate

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Return (Form 10 - Corporate Income Tax Return) with attached financial statements and schedules, filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; provisional tax computations are made semi-annually with interim payments due for the first half and second half of the fiscal year by corporations with a prior-year CIT liability
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); an approved extension of up to one month is possible for corporate groups requiring consolidated or audited financial statements; provisional tax payments are due by August 31 and February 28/29

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and tax classification information, including business registration number, legal entity name (Yuhan Hoesa), representative director, registered address, fiscal year start and end dates, and the tax jurisdiction classification box.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the entity as a domestic Korean corporation and LLC; complete the shareholder schedule listing all non-resident shareholders, their country of tax residence, TIN, shareholding percentage, and relationship. Failure to identify ultimate beneficial owners can trigger General Anti-Avoidance Rule review and denial of treaty benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Return type declaration: ordinary annual return, amended return, or assessment of tax after examination; also records whether the return is filed by a foreign-held domestic corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check the ordinary annual return box and, if any shareholder owns 10% or more, attach the foreign-invested company details. The Yuhan Hoesa will be treated as a Korean tax resident and must declare worldwide income; a non-resident shareholder does not file the Korean CIT return on behalf of the entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of total gross income and cost of sales, including all revenue derived from FDA 510(k) and European CE Mark regulatory consulting services, medical device registration work, quality system compliance fees, and other reimbursements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all global gross receipts, including wire transfers from overseas clients and fees collected through foreign credit-card payment rails. Cross-border consulting revenue cannot be treated as non-taxable foreign-source income merely because the payee is non-resident; the Korean LLC must recognize revenue on an accrual basis and maintain invoices, contracts, time sheets and delivery evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment section for non-deductible expenses, deductible temporary differences, tax-exempt income, and carryforward net operating losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back fines, penalties, excessive entertainment costs, gifts, unjustifiable donations, and payments to foreign related parties that lack economic substance. Any intercompany management fee, royalty, software license, or regulatory consulting fee paid to a non-resident affiliate must be justified with actual functions performed, personnel, and assets; a payment to a shell company with no CIGA in the foreign jurisdiction will be rejected and added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate tax base and statutory corporate income tax at progressive rates: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on income above KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% on income above KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% on income above KRW 300 billion; local income tax surcharge is 10% of the national CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the Yuhan Hoesa is organized in Korea, there is no separate non-resident corporate tax rate or territorial exemption. The entire global taxable income of the LLC is subject to Korean CIT. Foreign tax credits may be claimed for foreign withholding or income taxes paid on the LLC's foreign-source income only to the extent supported by foreign tax returns and Article 23 of the Tax Adjustment of International Transactions Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International transactions and transfer-pricing schedules, including the mandatory schedule of transactions with foreign related parties, foreign subsidiary details, loans, service fees, and transfer-pricing adjustment computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every cross-border related-party transaction irrespective of the presence or absence of profit repatriation. Report the country of the related party, transaction amount, pricing method applied (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split), and the functional/asset/risk profile of the counterparty. In the absence of a comparability analysis, the NTS may impute income under the arm's-length standard and impose a 30% adjustment penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax and profit-repatriation declaration section for dividends, interest, royalties, and other payments to non-resident shareholders or foreign payees during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean LLC declares or effectively distributes profits to non-resident shareholders, insert the distribution date, gross dividend amount, domestic withholding rate (20% CIT plus 2% local income tax, total 22%), and any DTA-reduced rate applied. Attach the Form for Claiming Withholding Tax Reduction/Exemption under a Tax Treaty, a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the shareholder's tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence of shareholding period. If treaty relief is rejected, arrears and delinquency interest will be assessed against the LLC as withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of preliminary corporate tax paid, tax credits, foreign tax credits, excess withholding credits, and refunds or additional payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter all semi-annual provisional payments already remitted to the NTS. For cross-border consulting revenue taxed in the source country, complete the foreign tax credit schedule and attach the foreign tax assessment notice; treaty-based credit relief is not automatic and requires a timely filed Korean return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director's declaration and signature section certifying that the return, schedules, and supporting financial statements are accurate, complete, and truthful.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The representative director of the Yuhan Hoesa must personally sign the declaration. Submitting false schedules, fabricating records, or concealing non-resident shareholders exposes the director to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and to piercing of the corporate veil for restitution of unpaid corporate taxes, penalties, and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual CIT return by the statutory deadline triggers an additional tax of 20% of the underpaid tax amount; where no tax is payable, a fixed penalty of up to KRW 1 million applies. Underreporting or overstating deductions generates a negligence surcharge equal to 10% of the unpaid tax, increased to 20% and up to 40% for fraudulent statements under Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Late payment of corporate tax causes daily delinquency surcharges plus additional collection interest. Where tax is evaded by fraud or false concealment, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act applies: imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines of up to 3 times the tax evaded. The NTS also blacklists tax evaders through the Public Notice System for High-Volume Tax Delinquents and may place directors on a travel ban.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% local income tax, making the aggregate statutory domestic rate 22%; a bilateral tax treaty may reduce the rate, typically to 10% to 15% depending on ownership and residency.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the withholding agent must submit, through the HomeTax portal or the appropriate NTS office, an Application for Withholding Tax Reduction or Exemption under the Tax Treaty together with the shareholder's current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a Beneficial Ownership Substantiation Statement, legal evidence of the shareholding percentage and holding period, and any additional treaty-specific declaration required by the relevant Korean-Korea bilateral DTA. The application must be made before or on the withholding remittance due date; if domestic-rate withholding has already been made, the non-resident shareholder may file a corrective withholding return or a refund claim within the statutory period supported by the same DTA package. Korean anti-abuse rules deny treaty benefits if the shareholder is a letterbox company without economic substance, beneficial ownership, or substantive activity in its residence country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The Korean statutory withholding rate on cross-border interest and royalty payments is 20% plus 2% local income tax, an aggregate effective rate of 22%. Many Korean bilateral tax treaties reduce interest withholding to approximately 10% and royalty withholding to 10% to 15%, but the reduced rate applies only to beneficial owners that satisfy the TRC and substance requirements. Royalties paid for patents, trademarks, know-how, and industrial/commercial/scientific equipment require complete license agreements and evidence of actual technology transfer to be eligible for treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, a Korean entity must prepare and submit a local (contemporaneous) transfer-pricing file where annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion, and a Master File where annual related-party transactions exceed KRW 100 billion; the international transaction report schedule must be attached to the corporate income tax return for all reportable cross-border related-party transactions, and documentation is required to satisfy the arm's-length standard even below the KRW 50 billion threshold if NTS requests justification.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean tax authorities apply a substance-over-form doctrine under Article 14 of the Corporate Tax Act and Articles 4 through 6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Transactions that lack commercial rationality and economic substance, or are arranged to take advantage of foreign shell entities, can be disregarded and recharacterized at arm's length. Core Income-Generating Activities are analyzed by reference to where the entity's staff, premises, capital, financial authority, and substantive decision-making reside; if the Yuhan Hoesa or its affiliate is a shell with no meaningful CIGA, the NTS can deny treaty benefits, apply controlled foreign corporation rules to passive income, impose adjustment penalties, and hold the managing director personally accountable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Tax Return and Corporate Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa receives consulting fees from overseas clients for FDA 510(k) and European CE Mark regulatory projects, but the invoices are omitted from Korean gross revenue, receipts are diverted to personal and foreign bank accounts, and fictitious expense invoices are issued by a non-resident shell supplier to reduce reported taxable profit to zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act. The fraudulent omission triggers an additional tax of 40% of the understated corporate tax plus local income tax surcharge, daily late-payment surcharges, and criminal prosecution. The director may be sentenced to imprisonment up to 5 years and ordered to pay fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the company is a sham or an alter ego of the director: the director becomes jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and civil restitution of diverted assets. The NTS transmits the director to the Justice authorities for blacklisting and travel-ban enforcement, and a criminal conviction brings imprisonment plus permanent disqualification from serving as a corporate director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-Pricing Misstatement and Inadequate International Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa deducts large management, consulting, and royalty payments to a Hong Kong or BVI related company that has no employees, no office, no assets, and no actual service performance, while failing to prepare or submit a Local File, Master File, or the Schedule of International Transactions to the NTS with the annual corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Articles 4, 5, 6 and 7 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The NTS may disregard the intercompany payments, re-determine taxable income at arm's length, impose an adjustment additional tax of up to 30% of the adjusted tax base, and add delinquency interest. Knowingly submitting false transfer-pricing schedules also falls within the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 3 times the avoided tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who knowingly signs false transfer-pricing documentation loses limited-liability protection; personal assets are reachable for the tax deficiency, penalties, and interest. The director is also subject to professional disqualification, blacklisting, travel ban, and criminal imprisonment for up to 5 years for aggravated fraudulent transfer-pricing violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Shell Company Abuse, and Unreported Cross-Border Accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa directs FDA/CE regulatory consulting fees to a tax-haven shell entity nominally owned by a non-resident trust, while the Korean managing director retains operating control and beneficial enjoyment of the funds; the director fails to disclose the foreign bank accounts and international wire activity to Korean customs, the Financial Services Commission, or the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, and the Act on the Registration and Reporting of Overseas Banking and Financial Accounts; penalties include up to 20% of the amount held in unreported foreign accounts, confiscation of the unreported accounts, and, for money-laundering or concealment through shell companies, imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million or up to three times the criminal proceeds, depending on the court's application.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because the shell entity is used as the alter ego of the director, the limited liability of the Yuhan Hoesa is disregarded. The director is personally liable for restitution of the converted funds and unpaid taxes, the Ministry of Justice imposes an exit restriction/blacklist, and a criminal conviction results in imprisonment, forfeiture of assets, and permanent damage to the director's legal capacity to manage corporate entities.
